contact-graspnet.value: An end-to-end network that efficiently generates a distribution of 6-DoF parallel-jaw grasps directly from a depth recording of a scene.

The grasp representation treats 3D points of the recorded point cloud as potential grasp contacts, rooting the full 6-DoF grasp pose and width in the observed point cloud to reduce the representation to 4-DoF.
Treat 3D points of the recorded point cloud as potential grasp contacts.
Root the full 6-DoF grasp pose and width in the observed point cloud, reducing dimensionality to 4-DoF.

Generating 6-DoF grasps from any viewpoint on structured clutter consisting of unknown objects, aiming for robust, diverse, and non-colliding grasps from a partially observable scene.

A method that takes a raw depth image (optionally with object masks) and produces 6-DoF grasp proposals with corresponding grasp widths, using per-point contact annotations to supervise a Contact Grasp Network.
An asymmetric Ushaped network built with set abstraction and feature propagation layers from PointNet++ for grasp prediction.
The network takes n=20000 random points p ∈ R^{20000×3} as input.
Grasps are predicted only for m=2048 farthest points of the input to fit GPU memory and ensure coverage.
The network has four heads, each with two 1D‑Conv layers, producing per‑point outputs s ∈ R^{?,10}.
Predicted grasp width ŵ_i ∈ [0, w_max] is split into 10 equidistant bins and represented by the center value of the bin(s) with highest confidence.
Approach direction a ∈ R^3 and baseline direction b ∈ R^3 are enforced orthonormal via an in‑network Gram‑Schmidt orthonormalization, predicting only the component â orthonormal to b.
The orthonormalization reduces the dimensionality of the predicted grasp representation and facilitates regression of 3D rotations.
Evaluate contact grasp success predictions ŝ ∈ R at all output points p_i using binary cross entropy.
Backpropagate only the top‑k point predictions with the largest errors l_bce,k, with k=512, to counteract data imbalance.
Evaluate geometry‑related predictions only at positive contact points p_i^+.
Combine predictions to the 6‑DoF grasp pose ĝ during training instead of supervising all network heads in isolation.
Define five 3D points v ∈ R^{5×3} representing the 6‑DoF gripper pose and transform them using ground‑truth and predicted grasp poses.
Formulate the 6‑DoF grasp loss l_add‑s as a weighted minimum average distance between gripper points v_gt and v_pred, accounting for gripper symmetry.
Weight each distance to the closest ground‑truth grasp point with the predicted contact success confidence ŝ_i.
Optimize a weighted, multi‑label binary cross entropy loss l_width for grasp width bin predictions, weighting bin losses anti‑proportional to bin size.
Combine losses into total loss l = α l_bce,k + β l_add‑s + γ l_width with α=1, β=10, γ=1.
